**Section D: Essay writing (10 marks).** Write an essay of between 250 and 300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 1.** "The African of the century": the government plans to issue a new stamp honouring the most influential man or woman of the 20th century. Write an essay on the person you think should receive this honour.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC sanctionne autant le respect du format imposé (essai biographique argumenté, discours structuré en constat/causes/solutions, article de magazine scolaire) que le contenu. Un essai sur « la personnalité du siècle » doit justifier le choix par des réalisations concrètes, pas seulement par la notoriété ; un discours de sensibilisation suit toujours la même progression en trois temps, décrire le problème, en expliquer les causes, puis proposer des solutions, jamais l'inverse ; un article sur un sujet controversé comme le châtiment corporel doit présenter les deux camps avant de conclure. Comme le sujet propose un choix, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun l'un des formats possibles.

## Topic 1 - Biographical essay (modèle, environ 270 mots)

If I had to choose one person to appear on a stamp honouring the most influential figure of the twentieth century, I would choose Nelson Mandela.

Mandela spent twenty-seven years in prison for opposing the apartheid system in South Africa, a regime that legally separated citizens by race and denied millions of people basic rights simply because of their skin colour. What makes his influence so exceptional is not only that he survived this ordeal, but what he chose to do once he was released in 1990.

Rather than seeking revenge against those who had imprisoned him, Mandela became President of South Africa in 1994 and worked to build a country where former oppressors and the formerly oppressed could live together. His Truth and Reconciliation Commission, which allowed victims and perpetrators of apartheid-era crimes to speak openly rather than pursuing endless cycles of retaliation, remains one of the most remarkable examples of political forgiveness in modern history.

Beyond South Africa, Mandela's story influenced how the entire world thinks about resisting injustice without resorting to hatred. He showed that a person can fight fiercely for what is right while still choosing dignity and reconciliation over bitterness, a lesson relevant far beyond the specific context of apartheid.

Other figures certainly changed the twentieth century, scientists, artists, political leaders of every kind, but few combined personal sacrifice, political achievement and moral example as completely as Mandela did. For a stamp meant to represent what humanity is capable of at its best, I cannot think of a more fitting face than his.

**Section D: Essay writing (10 marks).** Write an essay of between 250 and 300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 2.** As part of the celebration of Youth Week, you have been asked to deliver a speech on the problem of the numerous drug hawkers in our towns and villages. In your speech, you should describe the problem, explain the possible causes of the problem, and make a few suggestions on how the problem might be solved or at least alleviated.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Speech (modèle, environ 280 mots)

Dear friends,

As we celebrate Youth Week together, I want to talk about a problem many of us walk past every day without really seeing it: the growing number of drug hawkers in our towns and villages.

Anyone who has walked through our market recently has seen them: young men and women carrying baskets full of pills, selling medicine on the street corner as casually as someone would sell oranges or peanuts. Nobody checks what these pills actually contain, whether they suit the illness they are supposed to treat, or whether they have simply expired.

Why has this problem grown so much? Partly because unemployment leaves many young people with few honest ways to earn money, and selling drugs on the street requires no formal training or capital. Partly, too, because real pharmacies and hospitals remain too expensive or too far away for many families, who turn to hawkers out of necessity rather than choice. And partly because our laws against this illegal trade are rarely enforced with any real consistency.

So what can we do? First, we need affordable, accessible health centres in every neighbourhood, so that people are not forced to choose between an unqualified hawker and a hospital they cannot reach or afford. Second, our authorities must apply existing laws seriously and consistently, rather than only occasionally, so that this trade stops being worth the risk. Finally, we as young people can spread awareness among our own families and friends about the real dangers of unregulated medicine.

This problem will not disappear on its own. But if we understand its causes clearly, I believe we, as this generation's youth, are exactly the ones capable of pushing for the changes needed to solve it.

Thank you.

**Section D: Essay writing (10 marks).** Write an essay of between 250 and 300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 3.** Write an article for your school magazine on the use of corporal punishment in secondary schools. Your name is Mamadou. Your school magazine is called 'The Voice'. Give possible reasons for using or not using corporal punishment in schools.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - School magazine article (modèle, environ 260 mots)

**Should Corporal Punishment Still Have a Place in Our Schools?**

By Mamadou, for The Voice

Few topics divide opinion in our schools as sharply as corporal punishment. Should teachers still be allowed to cane students for misbehaviour, or is it time to leave this practice behind?

Those in favour argue that corporal punishment provides an immediate, clear consequence that students understand instantly, unlike detentions or written warnings that some students simply ignore. They also point out that many of today's most respected adults were themselves disciplined this way at school and turned out fine, suggesting the practice is not as harmful as critics claim.

Those against corporal punishment argue that it teaches students to avoid getting caught rather than to understand why their behaviour was wrong, since fear rarely produces genuine reflection. They also note that punishment is often applied unevenly, harder on students without connections or good relationships with staff, which turns discipline into something closer to intimidation than education. Finally, they argue that alternatives, such as community service within the school, guided reflection exercises or involving parents directly, can correct behaviour without relying on physical pain.

Personally, I lean towards ending corporal punishment, not because discipline does not matter, but because I believe our school can find consequences that teach responsibility rather than simply fear. A student who understands why cheating or bullying is wrong is less likely to repeat it than one who has merely learned to hide it better next time.

Whichever side you lean towards, this is a conversation our school community should have openly, rather than simply continuing old habits without ever questioning them.

### Piège à éviter
Sur un sujet aussi controversé que le châtiment corporel, défendre une seule position sans jamais mentionner les arguments de l'autre camp, alors que la consigne demande explicitement « give possible reasons for using or not using », fait perdre des points même si l'argumentation personnelle est solide.

### Conseil
Pour un article d'opinion sur un sujet de société controversé, présente toujours les deux camps avec la même rigueur avant de donner ton avis personnel : cela montre au correcteur une maturité de réflexion, même si ta conclusion penche clairement d'un côté.

incertitudes: Le sujet propose un choix entre trois formats différents dont un seul doit être traité le jour de l'examen ; les trois modèles fournis illustrent chacun un choix possible pour couvrir l'ensemble du barème.

Topic 1 est une question ouverte à réponse personnelle (« the person you think should receive this honour ») : Nelson Mandela est un choix plausible et solidement argumentable parmi d'autres personnalités du XXe siècle qui auraient également pu être défendues.
